// Generated policy companion for a private converted settings package.
// It deliberately supplies no renderer, persistence, HTTP handler, or backend.
package converted

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/mail"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

const (
	// BioLimit counts Unicode code points, not grapheme clusters.
	BioLimit = 240

	settingsRequestLimit  = 32 << 10
	settingsBioBytes      = 16 << 10
	settingsCountriesMax  = 64
	settingsCurrenciesMax = 64
	settingsRegionsMax    = 128
)

// settingsBioCodePoints measures the text a textarea exposes to a user. Form
// encoding expands each logical newline to CRLF, but the decoded draft remains
// raw so recovery can retain exactly what the transport supplied.
func settingsBioCodePoints(value string) int {
	return utf8.RuneCountInString(value) - strings.Count(value, "\r\n")
}

// SettingsValues is the application-owned state for the converted settings form.
// Empty fields are allowed unless the policy's selected options require a value.
type SettingsValues struct {
	Name, Bio, Email, Street, City, Region, Postal, Country, Currency string
	PublicEmail                                                       bool
}

type SettingsCountry struct {
	Code, Name string
	Regions    []string
}

type SettingsCurrency struct{ Code, Label string }

// SettingsPolicy owns copies of its configuration. Its snapshots may safely be
// handed to callers: modifying one cannot alter later validation.
type SettingsPolicy struct {
	countries  []SettingsCountry
	currencies []SettingsCurrency
	initial    SettingsValues
}

// SettingsValidation preserves submitted values so a caller can re-render them.
// FirstError is the first invalid field in authored focus order, or empty.
type SettingsValidation struct {
	Values     SettingsValues
	Errors     map[string]string
	FirstError string
}

func NewSettingsPolicy(countries []SettingsCountry, currencies []SettingsCurrency, initial SettingsValues) (*SettingsPolicy, error) {
	if len(countries) == 0 || len(countries) > settingsCountriesMax {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("settings policy: invalid country count")
	}
	if len(currencies) == 0 || len(currencies) > settingsCurrenciesMax {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("settings policy: invalid currency count")
	}
	ownedCountries := make([]SettingsCountry, len(countries))
	countryCodes := make(map[string]bool, len(countries))
	for i, country := range countries {
		if !settingsCode(country.Code, 16) || !settingsText(country.Name, 128, false) || countryCodes[country.Code] || len(country.Regions) == 0 || len(country.Regions) > settingsRegionsMax {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("settings policy: invalid or duplicate country")
		}
		countryCodes[country.Code] = true
		regions := make(map[string]bool, len(country.Regions))
		ownedCountries[i] = SettingsCountry{Code: country.Code, Name: country.Name, Regions: append([]string(nil), country.Regions...)}
		for _, region := range country.Regions {
			if !settingsText(region, 128, false) || regions[region] {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("settings policy: invalid or duplicate region")
			}
			regions[region] = true
		}
	}
	ownedCurrencies := make([]SettingsCurrency, len(currencies))
	currencyCodes := make(map[string]bool, len(currencies))
	for i, currency := range currencies {
		if !settingsCode(currency.Code, 16) || !settingsText(currency.Label, 128, false) || currencyCodes[currency.Code] {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("settings policy: invalid or duplicate currency")
		}
		currencyCodes[currency.Code] = true
		ownedCurrencies[i] = currency
	}
	if err := validateSettingsValues(initial); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("settings policy: invalid initial values: %w", err)
	}
	policy := &SettingsPolicy{countries: ownedCountries, currencies: ownedCurrencies, initial: initial}
	result, err := policy.Validate(initial)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("settings policy: invalid initial values: %w", err)
	}
	if result.FirstError != "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("settings policy: invalid initial %s: %s", result.FirstError, result.Errors[result.FirstError])
	}
	return policy, nil
}

func (p *SettingsPolicy) Countries() []SettingsCountry {
	if p == nil {
		return nil
	}
	result := make([]SettingsCountry, len(p.countries))
	for i, country := range p.countries {
		result[i] = SettingsCountry{Code: country.Code, Name: country.Name, Regions: append([]string(nil), country.Regions...)}
	}
	return result
}

func (p *SettingsPolicy) Currencies() []SettingsCurrency {
	if p == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return append([]SettingsCurrency(nil), p.currencies...)
}

func (p *SettingsPolicy) Initial() SettingsValues {
	if p == nil {
		return SettingsValues{}
	}
	return p.initial
}

// ParseSettingsValues admits only the named native form controls. It does not
// manufacture required text fields; membership and authored email rules belong to
// SettingsPolicy.Validate. The email rule is intentionally stricter than browser
// examples: when supplied it accepts only an ASCII addr-spec, with no display name
// and no whitespace normalization.
func ParseSettingsValues(values url.Values) (SettingsValues, error) {
	var result SettingsValues
	total := 0
	for key, entries := range values {
		total += len(key)
		if total > settingsRequestLimit {
			return result, fmt.Errorf("settings input: request exceeds limit")
		}
		switch key {
		case "name", "bio", "email", "email_is_public", "address", "city", "postal_code", "currency", "region", "country[code]":
		default:
			return result, fmt.Errorf("settings input: unknown field %q", key)
		}
		if len(entries) != 1 {
			return result, fmt.Errorf("settings input: field %q must occur once", key)
		}
		value := entries[0]
		total += len(value)
		if total > settingsRequestLimit {
			return result, fmt.Errorf("settings input: request exceeds limit")
		}
		if key == "email_is_public" {
			if value != "on" {
				return result, fmt.Errorf("settings input: invalid checkbox")
			}
			result.PublicEmail = true
			continue
		}
		if err := validateSettingsField(key, value); err != nil {
			return result, fmt.Errorf("settings input: %w", err)
		}
		switch key {
		case "name":
			result.Name = value
		case "bio":
			result.Bio = value
		case "email":
			result.Email = value
		case "address":
			result.Street = value
		case "city":
			result.City = value
		case "postal_code":
			result.Postal = value
		case "currency":
			result.Currency = value
		case "region":
			result.Region = value
		case "country[code]":
			result.Country = value
		}
	}
	return result, nil
}

// Validate applies the selected-option and authored email/bio policy without
// changing submitted values. Bio, email, country, region, and currency are kept in
// source focus order so a renderer can move focus deterministically.
func (p *SettingsPolicy) Validate(values SettingsValues) (SettingsValidation, error) {
	result := SettingsValidation{Values: values, Errors: make(map[string]string)}
	if err := validateSettingsValues(values); err != nil {
		return result, fmt.Errorf("settings values: %w", err)
	}
	if p == nil {
		result.Errors["country"] = "settings policy is unavailable"
		result.FirstError = "country"
		return result, nil
	}
	if err := validateSettingsField("bio", values.Bio); err != nil {
		result.Errors["bio"] = err.Error()
	} else if settingsBioCodePoints(values.Bio) > BioLimit {
		result.Errors["bio"] = fmt.Sprintf("must be at most %d Unicode code points", BioLimit)
	}
	if err := validateSettingsField("email", values.Email); err != nil {
		result.Errors["email"] = err.Error()
	} else if values.Email != "" && !settingsEmail(values.Email) {
		result.Errors["email"] = "must be an ASCII addr-spec"
	}
	country, found := p.country(values.Country)
	if err := validateSettingsField("country[code]", values.Country); err != nil {
		result.Errors["country"] = err.Error()
		found = false
	} else if !found {
		result.Errors["country"] = "must select a configured country"
	}
	if err := validateSettingsField("region", values.Region); err != nil {
		result.Errors["region"] = err.Error()
	} else if found {
		if !settingsMember(country.Regions, values.Region) {
			result.Errors["region"] = "must select a configured region"
		}
	} else if values.Region != "" {
		result.Errors["region"] = "cannot be used without a configured country"
	}
	if err := validateSettingsField("currency", values.Currency); err != nil {
		result.Errors["currency"] = err.Error()
	} else if !p.currency(values.Currency) {
		result.Errors["currency"] = "must select a configured currency"
	}
	for _, key := range []string{"bio", "email", "country", "region", "currency"} {
		if _, invalid := result.Errors[key]; invalid {
			result.FirstError = key
			break
		}
	}
	return result, nil
}

// RegionAfterCountryChange retains only a literal configured membership. It never
// chooses a replacement region on the application's behalf.
func (p *SettingsPolicy) RegionAfterCountryChange(code, current string) string {
	if country, ok := p.country(code); ok && settingsMember(country.Regions, current) {
		return current
	}
	return ""
}

func (p *SettingsPolicy) country(code string) (SettingsCountry, bool) {
	if p == nil {
		return SettingsCountry{}, false
	}
	for _, country := range p.countries {
		if country.Code == code {
			return country, true
		}
	}
	return SettingsCountry{}, false
}
func (p *SettingsPolicy) currency(code string) bool {
	if p == nil {
		return false
	}
	for _, currency := range p.currencies {
		if currency.Code == code {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
func settingsMember(options []string, value string) bool {
	for _, option := range options {
		if option == value {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func validateSettingsValues(values SettingsValues) error {
	for _, field := range []struct{ key, value string }{
		{"name", values.Name}, {"bio", values.Bio}, {"email", values.Email}, {"address", values.Street},
		{"city", values.City}, {"region", values.Region}, {"postal_code", values.Postal}, {"country[code]", values.Country}, {"currency", values.Currency},
	} {
		if err := validateSettingsField(field.key, field.value); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func validateSettingsField(key, value string) error {
	limit := map[string]int{"name": 512, "bio": settingsBioBytes, "email": 320, "address": 512, "city": 256, "region": 128, "postal_code": 64, "country[code]": 16, "currency": 16}[key]
	if len(value) > limit {
		return fmt.Errorf("%s exceeds byte limit", key)
	}
	if !utf8.ValidString(value) {
		return fmt.Errorf("%s has invalid UTF-8", key)
	}
	for _, r := range value {
		if unicode.IsControl(r) && !(key == "bio" && (r == '\n' || r == '\r' || r == '\t')) {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s has control data", key)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func settingsCode(value string, limit int) bool {
	if len(value) == 0 || len(value) > limit || !utf8.ValidString(value) {
		return false
	}
	for _, r := range value {
		if !(r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z' || r >= 'a' && r <= 'z' || r >= '0' && r <= '9' || r == '-' || r == '_') {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}
func settingsText(value string, limit int, empty bool) bool {
	if len(value) > limit || (!empty && strings.TrimSpace(value) == "") || !utf8.ValidString(value) {
		return false
	}
	for _, r := range value {
		if unicode.IsControl(r) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func settingsEmail(value string) bool {
	if strings.TrimSpace(value) != value || strings.Count(value, "@") != 1 {
		return false
	}
	local, domain, _ := strings.Cut(value, "@")
	if local == "" || len(local) > 64 || domain == "" || len(domain) > 253 || strings.HasPrefix(local, ".") || strings.HasSuffix(local, ".") || strings.Contains(local, "..") {
		return false
	}
	for _, r := range local {
		if !(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z' || r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z' || r >= '0' && r <= '9' || strings.ContainsRune(".!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-", r)) {
			return false
		}
	}
	for _, label := range strings.Split(domain, ".") {
		if label == "" || len(label) > 63 || label[0] == '-' || label[len(label)-1] == '-' {
			return false
		}
		for _, r := range label {
			if !(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z' || r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z' || r >= '0' && r <= '9' || r == '-') {
				return false
			}
		}
	}
	parsed, err := mail.ParseAddress(value)
	return err == nil && parsed.Name == "" && parsed.Address == value
}
